issue: PMAT-531 (closes forjar#531) — the v1.29.0 ledger booking, and the two false records the round found. The row is byte-identical to `release-goal.sh window v1.29.0` and is the FIRST any release has carried naming the paiml/forjar-cookbook commit it was qualified against (7c100454, PMAT-241). Three review lanes were unanimous that the cut's label moves were wrong: PMAT-233 reads `cancelled` and was carried into the next window (a treadmill), and PMAT-240 read `completed` with thirteen pipelines of its own shape still in scripts/ and neither acceptance criterion met. Both corrected; both gates that let them stand filed as PMAT-528 and PMAT-529. Correcting the false `completed` then pushed CB-2112 and CB-2114 over their ceilings — real growth, because a closed row became an open one — so CB-2114 was restored by real work and CB-2112 was RAISED with a written reason, which is when it became clear that 'MAY ONLY SHRINK' was a rule stated in the baseline's own text that nothing enforced.
recorded_at: after the round, the two corrections, the two tickets filed, and the raise arm the raise itself called for

quorum.rounds: one round of three sandboxed agy quorum lanes on the booking diff with --not-before pinned to the dispatch instant. All three returned, exits 0/0/0, durations 730s/430s/611s, verdicts 3/3 FAIL.
quorum.kill_rule: six claims about the row and the labels, plus the standing instruction that earned the previous round: quote any sentence or number a reader could check and find false. The unanimous finding was the one no gate asked — the label moves. The instructive one was a 2-1 SPLIT WHERE THE MINORITY WAS RIGHT: two lanes refuted the tickets list as missing three ids and the third confirmed it against the rule; the other two had found MENTIONS in PR bodies rather than shipped tickets. That is why every refutation is re-run instead of counted.
refuted_claims: That the cut's label moves are right — refuted 3/3 and both halves reproduce. PMAT-233 reads `cancelled` and its release: label was moved into the next window, which is a treadmill: every future cut carries it one further while gate T counts it as open work. PMAT-240 read `completed` and was moved as finished work that was never done.

That `status: completed` on PMAT-240 was true — thirteen pipelines of its own shape are still in scripts/ and NEITHER acceptance criterion had been met. It was planned when minted at f98b388d and completed by c5e4aaa3, flipped during unrelated work with no commit saying so. Corrected textually because `pmat work edit` refuses Completed -> Planned and Completed -> InProgress.

That no sentence in the record is checkable and false — PMAT-520's acceptance criteria said 'ten behaviour bullets' and 'twelve tickets' where the release shipped twelve and fifteen, and the ledger header's 'ten tags since the cookbook's master' became ELEVEN the moment v1.29.0 was tagged, which is a count that decays at every release.

That the booking is honestly a kind: triage change — CONFIRMED 3/3 when the lanes read it and made FALSE afterwards by this branch's own later work, which brought scripts/ratchets/cb21xx-baseline.json into the diff. Recorded as an EXPIRED confirmation rather than kept, and the receipt is kind: code with a falsification.
lane_errors: Two of three lanes refuted the `tickets` list as missing PMAT-200, PMAT-233 and PMAT-240, named in PR bodies. Does NOT reproduce: the window's rule is the first PMAT-<n> in the branch, then the title, then the body — the same rule gate A applies — and the row matches it exactly. What they found were MENTIONS; PR #517's body says 'eighteen more elsewhere are PMAT-240, census committed', which is a reference to future work. Measured: no commit between v1.28.0 and v1.29.0 names PMAT-240 as its subject. The third lane read the rule and confirmed the list.

The delegate stopped at its 30-turn limit while reducing, after all three lanes completed. Sixth occurrence in this session at that same point; worth a ticket in the paiml-implement repository rather than a seventh workaround.

crux.verdict: accept(the mechanism a ratchet needs is not the ceiling but the REASON a ceiling moved the wrong way, and every surveyed system requires one in writing rather than trusting the direction. Debian's Lintian overrides name the tag and the reason in a committed file [X]. Bazel's --incompatible_* flags name the release at which a tolerated breakage stops being tolerated [X]. Nix pins a stale derivation with an explicit comment rather than silently [X]. SLSA records the level a project MEETS and requires evidence to claim a higher one [X]. forjar's baseline has carried a `justification` field since it was written and nothing read it, so a one-character edit turned every future regression green. Where forjar is still WORSE: none of the four lets the author of the change be the only reviewer of its reason, and this gate does — the justification is written and read by the same hand until a human opens the PR.)
